s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with migration to the right lower quadrant

Voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
key_facts: Abdominal pain began around the umbilicus 2 days prior

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Classic presentation of abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, elevated white-cell count, and imaging findings compatible with appendicitis

shortlist.label: Plastron appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound assessment specifically mentioned compatibility with plastron appendicitis, a rare form of appendicitis

shortlist.label: Perforated appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays and elevated white-cell count suggest possible perforation

shortlist.label: Cecal diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Location of pain and tenderness in the right lower quadrant, along with imaging findings, could also suggest cecal diverticulitis

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and imaging findings could also be consistent with Meckel's diverticulitis, a rare but important differential diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including abdominal pain that migrated to the right lower quadrant, elevated white-cell count, and imaging findings, are consistent with acute appendicitis. The ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis and computed tomography showing a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Plastron appendicitis
rejected.why: While the ultrasound assessment was compatible with plastron appendicitis, this term is not a standard medical diagnosis and is likely referring to a specific appearance of appendicitis on imaging.

rejected.label: Perforated appendicitis
rejected.why: There is no free air under the diaphragm on plain abdominal X-rays, which makes perforation less likely.

rejected.label: Cecal diverticulitis
rejected.why: The computed tomography findings are more consistent with appendicitis than diverticulitis, and there is no mention of a diverticulum.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: The location of the pain and imaging findings are more consistent with appendicitis, and there is no mention of a Meckel's diverticulum.
